items.title: T cells gone viral: New study finds host genetics shape the brain's immune response to chronic herpesvirus infection
items.text: Scientists have long suspected a common human herpesvirus contributed to the development of multiple sclerosis, a disease affecting the central nervous system and a leading cause of disability in young adults. A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) demonstrates genetically determined differences in host control of a similar herpesvirus in mice are a major risk factor for allowing T cells to enter the brain and may offer clues to why only a fraction of the population infected with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) develops MS.
